program_overview.title: Microsoft Office and Windows for Kids
program_overview.tagline: The digital skills school quietly assumes: real Word documents, presentations that earn applause, first spreadsheets, and tidy digital habits, learned properly at 7 to 12.
program_overview.description:
Schools assume children can format a document, build a presentation and manage their files, but nobody actually teaches it. This live online course does, properly, for children aged 7 to 12: Windows fundamentals and tidy file habits, digital art with the built-in creative tools, real Microsoft Word skills, PowerPoint presentations with restraint and style, first Excel spreadsheets with formulas and charts, and OneNote and Teams, the tools their school life increasingly runs on.

Everything is project-based: children produce school reports, posters, family newsletters, quiz presentations, pocket-money trackers and a final integrated project they present at demo day. The pace is honest and kid-sized: five months of teaching at two live classes a week, with a sixth month in hand for children who need more practice. Classwork in every session, a small homework task after every class, a mixed challenge at each month’s end, and a final exam, a project demo plus a friendly practical test, that decides the certificate. Real skills, really tested, immediately useful at school.
what_makes_this_different: Project-based from week one: real school reports, presentations and trackers, not button tours
Current tools, honestly taught: Windows 11, the free Office web apps, Photos and Clipchamp, no outdated software
Typing and file hygiene built in: the quiet skills that make every later computer subject easier
Kid-sized honest pace: 5 months at 2 classes a week, with a 6th month in hand when needed
Real assessment, gently done: monthly mixed challenges and a final practical exam that decides the certificate, with a free retest after revision
Small live batches capped at 10, grouped by age, with mini-batch and 1-on-1 options

learning_path.month_2: Word (Weeks 5-8): documents that look professional, from formatting to images and tables

Typing, file management and digital habits that compound for years
First data skills: a child who can put numbers in a sheet and make an honest chart
A confident step into our coding courses, where these computer habits quietly pay off

month_1.title: Month 1: Windows Basics & Digital Art
month_1.description: Windows fundamentals, tidy file habits, and creative confidence with Paint, Photos and Clipchamp.

week_1.title: Introduction to Windows & Computer Basics
topics: Computer components: monitor, keyboard, mouse, CPU
Mouse skills: click, double-click, right-click, drag
Keyboard basics: letters, numbers, special keys
Caps Lock, Shift, Enter, Backspace, Delete
week_1.practice: Practice starting up and shutting down the computer the right way, then pin your three favorite apps to the taskbar and show a parent.

week_2.title: File Management & Organization
projects: Create organized folder system for schoolwork
week_2.practice: Create a folder tree for your school subjects and sort five files into the right folders using cut, copy and paste.

week_3.title: Microsoft Paint Fundamentals
topics: Saving in different formats (PNG, JPEG, BMP)
week_3.practice: Draw your dream treehouse in Paint using at least four different tools and the fill bucket.

week_4.title: Photos, Clipchamp and Creative Projects
topics: Editing pictures with the Windows Photos app
Cropping, lighting and honest photo fixes
Clipchamp: first video edits with clips and titles
Saving projects where you can find them again
A creative mini-showcase for the family
projects: Edited photo set: before and after
A 60-second family slideshow video in Clipchamp
week_4.practice: Make one tiny video about your week
week_4.assessment: Month 1 check: a files-and-creativity challenge mixing everything so far

month_2.title: Month 2: Microsoft Word Mastery
month_2.description: Become a Word expert, creating professional documents, reports, and creative writing projects.

week_5.title: Word Basics & Text Formatting
topics: Opening Microsoft Word and interface tour
week_5.practice: Type a short paragraph about your favorite animal in Word and format it with two fonts, one color and bold key words.

week_6.title: Advanced Formatting & Page Layout
week_6.practice: Make a one page mini newsletter about your week using two columns, a header and a page border.

week_7.title: Working with Images & Graphics
week_7.practice: Insert three pictures into a 'My Hobbies' document, then crop one, style another and wrap text around the third.

week_8.title: Tables, References & Collaboration
week_8.practice: Build your weekly class timetable as a Word table and give the header row its own color.
week_8.assessment: Month 2 check: format a document live from a messy draft, plus a mixed quiz reaching back to month 1

month_3.title: Month 3: PowerPoint Presentation Excellence
month_3.description: Master the art of creating engaging, professional presentations with PowerPoint.

week_9.title: PowerPoint Fundamentals
week_9.practice: Create a four slide PowerPoint about your favorite place using one theme and tidy bullet points.

week_10.title: Animations & Transitions
week_10.practice: Add a different transition to each slide of your deck and give the title text an entrance animation.

week_11.title: Multimedia & Interactive Elements
week_11.practice: Add a photo album slide, one short video and a little background music to your presentation.

week_12.title: Advanced Design & Presenting
week_12.practice: Design a custom layout in Slide Master, then rehearse presenting your deck out loud for two minutes.
week_12.assessment: Month 3 check: build and present three slides live, with mixed questions from earlier months

month_4.title: Month 4: Excel and Data Skills
month_4.description: Learn spreadsheet basics, data management, charts, and basic formulas with Excel.

week_13.title: Excel Basics & Data Entry
week_13.practice: Enter a pretend week of family fruit shopping into Excel and use AutoFill to complete the days of the week.

week_14.title: Formulas & Functions
week_14.practice: Track your pocket money for an imaginary week, then total it with SUM and find the daily average with AVERAGE.

week_15.title: Charts & Data Visualization
week_15.practice: Turn your favorite game or sports scores into a column chart and a pie chart, each with a proper title and labels.

week_16.title: Data Management & Analysis
week_16.practice: Sort a list of ten pretend test scores from highest to lowest and use conditional formatting to highlight the top three.
week_16.assessment: Month 4 check: a mini spreadsheet challenge with formulas and one chart, plus mixed revision

month_5.title: Month 5: OneNote, Teams and the Grand Finale
month_5.description: The organizational tools school life runs on, one integrated project that uses everything, and the final exam.

week_17.title: OneNote Digital Notebook
week_17.practice: Set up a OneNote notebook with one section per school subject and fill one page with notes plus a small drawing.

week_18.title: Microsoft Teams for Students
week_18.practice: With a parent, practice joining a video call, sending one polite chat message and sharing your screen for a minute.

week_19.title: The Integrated Project
week_19.practice: Embed an Excel chart of your scores or savings into a Word report and write two sentences explaining what it shows.

week_20.title: Final Exam and Demo Day
week_20.practice: Write a mini plan for your final project: what you will make, which Office apps you will use and your three work sessions.
week_20.assessment: FINAL EXAM: a practical test across Word, PowerPoint and Excel plus the integrated project demo. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest

faqs.question: What will my child learn in this course?
faqs.answer: Real, school-ready digital skills: Windows confidence and tidy file habits, photo editing and first videos with the free Photos and Clipchamp apps, professional documents in Word, presentations with actual design sense in PowerPoint, first spreadsheets with formulas and charts in Excel, and OneNote and Teams for school organization. Everything is learned by making real things: reports, posters, trackers and a final integrated project.

faqs.question: Which age group is this designed for?
faqs.answer: Ages 7 to 12, with batches grouped by age so the pace and examples fit the room. No prior computer experience is needed; the course starts at the desktop and the mouse and builds up patiently.

faqs.question: How long does it take a child to learn Microsoft Office?
faqs.answer: To real, school-ready capability: 5 months at 2 live classes a week plus an hour or two of practice. The course keeps a 6th month in hand for children who need more repetition, with no rushing and no penalty. Skills show up at school almost immediately, the first properly formatted report usually appears within month 2.

faqs.question: How is my child assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. There is classwork in every session, a small homework task after every class, and a mixed challenge at the end of each month that deliberately revisits earlier skills so they stop fading. The course ends with a final practical exam plus a project demo. Passing earns the certificate; a child who falls short gets focused revision and a free retest. Gentle in tone, real in standard.

faqs.question: Does my child need computer experience before starting?
faqs.answer: No. Month 1 begins with the absolute basics: using Windows, organizing files and folders, and simple digital art in Paint. Everything builds step by step from there.

faqs.question: What software does my child need at home?
faqs.answer: A Windows computer with internet is enough. The free Office web versions of Word, PowerPoint, Excel and OneNote cover the whole course, and we use them alongside free built-in tools like Photos, Clipchamp and the Snipping Tool. If your family already has desktop Office or Microsoft 365, your child can use that too; nothing needs to be purchased.

faqs.question: How does this help with school, and what comes next?
faqs.answer: The skills map directly to schoolwork: essays and reports in Word, class presentations in PowerPoint, and data projects in Excel. Afterwards, many students move into our Scratch or kids coding courses, since comfortable computer use makes learning to code much smoother.

faqs.question: What is the fee structure?
faqs.answer: Group batches cost ₹1,499 per month and include 2 classes each week with at most 10 children. A mini batch of 3-4 students is ₹2,999 per month, while personal 1-on-1 coaching with 2 private classes weekly is ₹4,999 per month. Families outside India pay a price set for their own country, shown on this page in their local currency.

faqs.question: Can my child attend a trial class first?
faqs.answer: Yes, the first step for every family is a free demo class, booked at learn.modernagecoders.com/contact. There is no commitment attached, and parents can sit in to see exactly how the teacher works with kids.

faqs.question: What do the classes look like?
faqs.answer: Each class is a live 1-hour online session with a real teacher guiding a small group, never a pre-recorded video. Children practice hands-on in the actual software during class and get help the moment they are stuck.

faqs.question: Will my child receive a certificate?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is earned: the certificate is awarded on passing the final exam, a practical test across Word, PowerPoint and Excel plus the integrated project demo, with a free retest after revision if the first attempt falls short. Alongside it stands a portfolio of 20+ real documents, presentations and spreadsheets.
